title: RxJS Practice
description: Practise the twelve ideas in this RxJS course. Choose an answer, then read why it fits the example.

exercises.question: What does subscribe do?
exercises.explanation: An observable sends values to a subscriber. of makes a stream from the values you give it.

exercises.question: Which operator transforms each value?
exercises.explanation: map changes each emitted value into a new value. pipe connects an operator to the stream.

exercises.question: What happens to a value whose filter test is false?
exercises.explanation: filter allows values through only when its test is true. Other values are left out.

exercises.question: What does take(2) count?
exercises.explanation: take limits how many values a subscriber receives. It completes after that number has arrived.

exercises.question: What is interval's first emitted number?
exercises.explanation: interval emits a growing count at a chosen time gap. Its first value is zero, after the first gap.

exercises.question: How many clicks does this subscription handle?
exercises.explanation: fromEvent listens to events from a target. Each matching event becomes a stream value.

exercises.question: What does unsubscribe stop?
options: This subscription's listening and associated work
Every JavaScript program on the computer
exercises.explanation: A subscription has an unsubscribe method. Calling it stops that subscription and runs the source cleanup.

exercises.question: Who gets a plain Subject's new value?
exercises.explanation: A Subject is both something you can subscribe to and something you can send values into. It shares new values with current subscribers.

exercises.question: What does this late subscriber receive first?
exercises.explanation: A BehaviorSubject starts with one value and gives the latest value to each new subscriber.

exercises.question: When can combineLatest first emit?
options: Before any input has a value
After every input has emitted at least once
exercises.explanation: combineLatest waits until each input has a value, then emits their latest values together when either changes.

exercises.question: What happens to the previous inner stream?
options: It is unsubscribed when a new one is chosen
It always finishes and replaces the newest result
exercises.explanation: switchMap switches to a new inner stream and unsubscribes from the previous one. It is useful when only the newest request matters.

exercises.question: What must catchError return here?
exercises.explanation: catchError can replace a failed stream with another observable. A fallback can give the caller a useful value instead of an unhandled failure.
